units.literal: In praise: civil and martial regalia blaze bright; ritual forms stand solemn and still.

units.zh: 分別禮數，莫過輿服。
units.en: To mark ritual rank, nothing exceeds carriages and dress.
units.literal: To distinguish ritual grades, nothing surpasses carriages and dress.

units.zh: 「漆畫牽車」注「戍棟樑」，一本「戍」作「戈」。
units.en: On the "lacquer-painted traction carriage," the gloss reads "defense ridgebeam"; one edition reads shu as ge ("halberd").
units.literal: On the "lacquer-painted traction carriage," the gloss reads "defense ridgebeam"; in one edition shu is written as ge ("halberd").

units.zh: 「輿車」注「成校棟樑」，一本「成校」作「戈杖」。
units.en: On the "carriage vehicle," the gloss reads "completion-correction ridgebeam"; one edition reads cheng-xiao as gezhang ("halberd staff").
units.literal: On the "carriage vehicle," the gloss reads "completion-correction ridgebeam"; in one edition cheng-xiao is written as gezhang ("halberd staff").

units.zh: 「衣書車」注「刺代棟樑」，「平乘車」注「刺代棟樑」，並疑。
units.en: On the "book-and-robe carriage" and the "level-riding carriage," each gloss reads "pierce-substitute ridgebeam"—both are doubtful.
units.literal: On the "book-and-robe carriage," the gloss reads "pierce-substitute ridgebeam"; on the "level-riding carriage," the gloss reads "pierce-substitute ridgebeam"—both are doubtful.

units.en: [1] Endnote marker.
units.literal: [1] Endnote marker.

units.zh: 姚興
units.en: Biography of Yao Xing.
units.literal: Yao Xing.

units.zh: 姚興，字子略，萇之長子也。
units.en: Yao Xing, courtesy Zilüe, was the firstborn of Yao Chang.
units.literal: Yao Xing, style name Zilüe, was Yao Chang's eldest son.

units.zh: 萇之在馬牧，興自長安冒難奔萇，萇立為皇太子。
units.en: While Yao Chang was raising troops in the pastures, Yao Xing slipped out of Chang'an through danger to join him and was named heir.
units.literal: When Chang was at the horse pastures, Xing braved peril from Chang'an and fled to Chang; Chang established him as crown prince.

units.zh: 碩德曰：「太子志度寬明，必無疑阻。
units.en: Yao Shuode replied, "The heir is open-minded; he will not mistrust us.
units.literal: Shuo De said: "The crown prince's aims and measure are generous and clear; there will surely be no suspicion or obstruction.

units.zh: 興自稱大將軍，以尹緯為長史，狄伯支為司馬，率眾伐苻登。
units.en: Yao Xing took the title grand general, appointed Yin Wei and Di Bozhi, and marched against Fu Deng.
units.literal: Xing styled himself grand general, made Yin Wei chief clerk, Di Bozhi marshal, and led the host to attack Fu Deng.

units.zh: 太元十九年，僭即帝位於槐里，大赦境內，改元曰皇初，遂如安定。
units.en: In Taiyuan 19 he declared himself emperor at Huaili, amnestied his realm, took the reign name Huangchu, and moved to Anding.
units.literal: In the nineteenth year of Taiyuan he unlawfully assumed the imperial dignity at Huaili, granted a general amnesty within his borders, changed the era name to Huangchu, and proceeded to Anding.

units.zh: 登眾甚盛，興慮詳不能遏，乃自將精騎以迫登，遣尹緯領步卒赴詳。
units.en: Fearing Fu Deng's numbers, Yao Xing rode out with elite horse and sent Yin Wei to reinforce Yao Xiang.
units.literal: Deng's host was very strong; Xing feared Xiang could not stop him, and personally led picked cavalry to press Deng, dispatching Yin Wei to lead foot soldiers to reinforce Xiang.

units.zh: 與其中舍人梁喜、洗馬範勖等講論經籍，不以兵難廢業，時人咸化之。
units.en: With Liang Xi, Fan Xu, and other staff he kept debating the classics despite the war, and the capital gentry took his example.
units.literal: With his household gentleman Liang Xi, groom Fan Xu, and others he lectured and discussed the classics and records, and because of military hardship did not abandon study; people of the time were all transformed by it.

units.zh: 苻堅時為太子舍人。
units.en: Under Fu Jian he served as attendant to the crown prince.
units.literal: In Fu Jian's time he was a gentleman attendant at the heir apparent's palace.

units.zh: 及鎮長安，甚有威惠。
units.en: As regent in Chang'an he combined stern authority with generous rule.
units.literal: When he garrisoned Chang'an, he had great awe-inspiring kindness.

units.zh: 萇死，興秘不發喪，以其叔父緒鎮安定，碩德鎮陰密，弟崇守長安。
units.en: Yao Xing hid his father's death, posting Yao Xu at Anding, Yao Shuode at Yinmi, and his brother Yao Chong in Chang'an.
units.literal: When Chang died, Xing kept it secret and did not announce mourning; he had his uncle Xu garrison Anding, Shuo De garrison Yinmi, and his younger brother Chong defend Chang'an.

units.zh: 興乃發喪行服。
units.en: Only then did Yao Xing proclaim his father's death and don mourning.
units.literal: Xing thereupon announced mourning and observed the rites of bereavement.

units.zh: 興自安定如涇陽，與登戰于山南，斬登。
units.en: Yao Xing advanced from Anding to Jingyang and slew Fu Deng south of the range.
units.literal: Xing from Anding went to Jingyang, fought Deng south of the mountain, and beheaded Deng.

units.zh: 封征虜緒為晉王，征西碩德為隴西王，征南靖等及功臣尹緯、齊難、楊佛嵩等並為公侯，其餘封爵各有差。
units.en: He made Yao Xu prince of Jin, Yao Shuode prince of Longxi, and ennobled Jing together with meritorious subjects Yin Wei, Qi Nan, Yang Fosong, and others as dukes or marquises.
units.literal: He enfeoffed the General Who Conquers Barbarians Xu as Prince of Jin, the General Who Conquers the West Shuo De as Prince of Longxi, the General Who Conquers the South Jing and others together with meritorious subjects Yin Wei, Qi Nan, Yang Fosong, and others all as dukes or marquises; the remaining enfeoffments each had their gradations.

units.zh: 興追尊其庶母孫氏為皇太后，配饗太廟。
units.en: He posthumously titled his concubine-mother Lady Sun empress dowager and enshrined her with the ancestors.
units.literal: Xing posthumously honored his concubine mother Lady Sun as empress dowager and paired her for sacrifice in the Grand Temple.

units.zh: 鮮卑越質詰歸率戶二萬叛乞伏乾歸，降於興，興處之于成紀，拜使持節、鎮西將軍、平襄公。
units.en: Yuezhi Jiegui brought twenty thousand households from Qifu Gangui to Yao Xing, who settled them at Chengji and titled him general who guards the west, duke of Pingxiang.
units.literal: The Xianbei Yuezhi Jiegui led twenty thousand households in revolt from Qifu Gangui and surrendered to Xing; Xing settled them at Chengji and appointed him Bearer of the Imperial Insignia, General Who Guards the West, and Duke of Pingxiang.

units.zh: 萇出征討，常留統後事。
units.en: Yao Chang habitually left him in charge of the rear whenever he marched.
units.literal: Whenever Chang went out on campaign, he regularly left him behind to oversee rear affairs.

units.zh: 咸陽太守劉忌奴據避世堡以叛，興襲忌奴，擒之。
units.en: Liu Jinu of Xianyang held Bishi fort in revolt; Yao Xing stormed it and took him prisoner.
units.literal: The Administrator of Xianyang Liu Jinu occupied Bishi Fort in rebellion; Xing raided Jinu and captured him.

units.zh: 登因急攻緯，緯將出戰，興馳遣狄伯支謂緯曰：「兵法不戰而制人者，蓋為此也。
units.en: As Fu Deng stormed Yin Wei's line, Yao Xing sent Di Bozhi with a warning: "The sage general wins without fighting—this is such a case.
units.literal: Deng thereupon urgently attacked Wei; Wei was about to go out to battle when Xing swiftly sent Di Bozhi to tell Wei: "The art of war's subduing others without fighting—this is what it is for.

units.zh: 苻登窮寇，宜持重，不可輕戰。」
units.en: Fu Deng is desperate; stand fast and do not risk a rash clash."
units.literal: Fu Deng is a cornered bandit; you ought to hold firm and not fight lightly."

units.zh: 散其部眾，歸復農業。
units.en: He disbanded Fu Deng's troops to the plow.
units.literal: He scattered Deng's following and returned them to agriculture.

units.zh: 徙陰密三萬戶于長安，分大營戶為四，置四軍以領之。
units.en: He resettled thirty thousand Yinmi households in Chang'an, split the great camp into four armies, and assigned commanders.
units.literal: He moved thirty thousand households of Yinmi to Chang'an, divided the great camp households into four, and set up four armies to command them.

units.zh: 興率諸將討之，軍次武功，多兄子良國殺多而降。
units.en: Yao Xing marched to suppress them; at Wugong Yang Duo's nephew Liangguo killed him and surrendered.
units.literal: Xing led the generals to punish them; the army halted at Wugong; Duo's elder brother's son Liangguo killed Duo and surrendered.

units.zh: 晉武帝具禮護送。
units.en: Emperor Wu of Jin honored him with full ceremony and sent him homeward under escort.
units.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin treated him with full rites and escorted him on his way.

units.zh: 雖復遣家入質，子陽之態轉遒；
units.en: Though he again sent his family as hostages, his manner grew only fiercer, like Ziyang;
units.literal: Though again he sent his family as hostages, Ziyang's manner grew only fiercer;

units.zh: 俄而荊州刺史沈攸之作亂，高帝謂淹曰：「天下紛紛若是，君謂何如？」
units.en: Soon Jing inspector Shen Youzhi rose in arms; Gaodi asked Yan, "The world is chaos like this—what is your view?"
units.literal: Before long Jing inspector Shen Youzhi rebelled; Gaodi said to Yan, "The realm is in such turmoil—what do you think?"

units.zh: 昇明初，齊帝輔政，聞其才，召爲尚書駕部郎、驃騎參軍事。
units.en: At the start of Ascendant Bright, with Qi's emperor as regent, he heard of Yan and made him secretariat director of the imperial equipage and valiant-cavalry staff officer.
units.literal: At the start of the Ascendant Bright era, when Qi's emperor held regency, he heard of Yan's talent and summoned him as Masters of Writing director of the imperial equipage and valiant-cavalry staff officer.

units.zh: 太祖高皇帝篤猶子之愛，降家人之慈；
units.en: Grand Ancestor Gao cherished a nephew as a son and gave the kindness of kin under one roof;
units.literal: Grand Ancestor Emperor Gao cherished the love due a nephew-son and granted the kindness shown within a household;

units.zh: 駙馬都尉置由漢武，[9]或以假諸功臣，或以加於戚屬，是以魏曹植表駙馬、奉車趣為一號。
units.en: The consort commandant was created by Han Wudi; [9] it was sometimes given to meritorious ministers and sometimes to kin—hence Cao Zhi in Wei asked to merge consort commandant and carriage attendant into one title.
units.literal: The post of Commandant of the Consort's Carriage was established by Emperor Wu of Han; [9] sometimes it was lent to meritorious ministers, sometimes added for kin—hence in Wei, Cao Zhi petitioned to make the consort commandant and the carriage attendant a single title.

units.zh: 駙馬都尉置由漢武 「由」字原本漫漶，今據各本補。
units.en: On "consort commandant established by Han Wudi": the character you was faded in the base text and is restored from other editions.
units.literal: The post of Commandant of the Consort's Carriage was established by Emperor Wu of Han—the character "by" in the original was effaced; it is now supplied from the various editions.

units.zh: 年二十，遭王莽敗，世祖即位於冀州。
units.en: At twenty he lived through Wang Mang's fall and watched Liu Xiu raise the Han banner in Ji.
units.literal: At twenty he encountered Wang Mang's collapse, and the Founding Ancestor took the throne in Ji Province.

units.zh: 宋武創業，依擬古典，神州部內，不復別封。
units.en: When Emperor Wu of Song founded the dynasty on ancient models, he ceased granting separate fiefs within the imperial domain.
units.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song founded the dynasty, following ancient models, within the imperial domain he no longer enfeoffed separately.

units.zh: 於是諸侯王及 太尉長安侯臣綰等三百人，與博士稷嗣君叔孫通謹擇良日二月甲午，上尊號。
units.en: So the feudal lords and Grand Marshal, Marquis of Chang'an, Wan, and 300 others, together with the Erudite Lord Jisi, Shusun Tong, carefully chose an auspicious day, the jiawu day of the second month, and presented the honored title.
units.literal: So the feudal lords and Grand Marshal Lord Chang'an Chen Wan and 300 others, together with Erudite Ji, Successor Lord Shu Sun Tong, carefully chose an auspicious day, the jiawu day of the second month, and presented the honored title.

units.zh: 天下既定，命蕭何次律令，韓信申軍法，張蒼定章程，叔孫通制禮儀，陸賈造新語。
units.en: After the world was settled, he commanded Xiao He to arrange the statutes and commands, Han Xin to explain military law, Zhang Cang to establish procedures, Shusun Tong to create rituals and ceremonies, Lu Jia to compose new discourses.
units.literal: After the world was settled, he commanded Xiao He to arrange the statutes and commands, Han Xin to explain military law, Zhang Cang to establish procedures, Shu Sun Tong to create rituals and ceremonies, Lu Jia to compose new discourses.

units.zh: 春正月，追尊兄伯號曰武哀侯。
units.en: In the first month of spring, he posthumously honored his elder brother with the title Lord Wu'ai.
units.literal: In the first month of spring, he posthumously honored his elder brother with the title Lord Wu'ai.

units.zh: 遙光敗，入東昏宮。
units.en: When Yaoguang fell, she was taken into the Depraved Emperor's palace.
units.literal: When Yaoguang was defeated, she entered the Depraved Emperor's palace.

units.zh: 至乎晉初，爰定新禮，荀顗制之於前，摯虞刪之於末。
units.en: At the beginning of Jin, a new ritual code was established: Xun Yi drafted it at the outset, and Zhi Yu revised it at the end.
units.literal: Reaching the beginning of Jin, then the new rites were fixed — Xun Yi formulated them at the start, Zhi Yu edited them at the end.

units.zh: 永明初，衛將軍王儉領丹陽尹，復引爲主簿。
units.en: Early in Yongming, Wang Jian of the guards, as Danyang intendant, drew him back as chief clerk.
units.literal: Early Yongming, General of the Guards Wang Jian took Danyang as intendant and again recruited him as chief clerk.

units.zh: 十一月，青州黃巾寇太山，太山太守應劭擊破之。
units.en: In the eleventh month Qingzhou Yellow Turbans invaded Taishan; Ying Shao, the governor, drove them off.
units.literal: In the eleventh month, the Qingzhou Yellow Turbans raided Mount Tai, and Mount Tai Governor Ying Shao attacked and defeated them.

units.zh: 秋七月，司空种拂免，光祿大夫濟南淳于嘉為司空。
units.en: In the seventh month Chong Fu left the ministry of works; Chunyu Jia of Jinan, grandee of brilliant candidacy, replaced him.
units.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Minister of Works Chong Fu was dismissed, and Grandee of Brilliant Candidacy Chunyu Jia of Jinan was made Minister of Works.

units.zh: 六世祖猛，秦苻堅丞相，家於華山之鄜城。
units.en: His sixth-generation ancestor Meng had been chancellor under Fu Jian of Former Qin; the family settled at Fucheng in Huashan.
units.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Meng was chancellor under Fu Jian of Former Qin; the family settled at Fucheng in Huashan.

units.zh: 及石季龍死，裒上表請伐之，即日戒嚴，直指泗口。
units.en: After Shi Hu’s death Chu Pou memorialized for an expedition; the army mobilized the same day toward Sikou.
units.literal: When Shi Jilong died, Pou submitted a memorial requesting to campaign against his state; that very day martial law was declared, aiming straight at Sikou.

units.zh: 時石季龍新死，其國大亂，遺戶二十萬口渡河，將歸順，乞師救援。
units.en: Shi Hu had just died and his state was in chaos; two hundred thousand people crossed the Yellow River seeking Jin protection and begging for an army.
units.literal: At the time Shi Jilong had newly died; his state was greatly in chaos; leftover households two hundred thousand mouths crossed the river, about to submit in allegiance, begging troops for rescue.

units.zh: 順皇帝諱準，字仲謀，[1]小字智觀，明帝第三子也。
units.en: Emperor Shun, taboo name Zhun, courtesy name Zhongmou, [1] childhood name Zhiguan, was the third son of Emperor Ming.
units.literal: Emperor Shun, taboo name Zhun, courtesy name Zhongmou, [1] childhood name Zhiguan, was the third son of Emperor Ming.

units.zh: 遷司徒刑獄參軍事，入爲尚書殿中郎，轉司徒竟陵王記室參軍，以父憂去職。
units.en: He rose to prison staff in the criminal office, then palace attendant in the secretariat, then recorder to the Prince of Jingling, and left for his father's mourning.
units.literal: Promoted to Criminal Office Prison staff officer, entered as Attendant of the Palace Department in the Masters of Writing, then transferred to Staff Officer and Recorder to the Prince of Jingling of the Secretariat, left office for father's mourning.

units.zh: 始高祖與昉遇竟陵王西邸，從容謂昉曰：「我登三府，當以卿爲記室。」
units.en: When Gaozu first met Fang at the Prince of Jingling's western residence, he said lightly, "When I reach the three offices, you shall be my recorder."
units.literal: When Gaozu first met Fang at the Prince of Jingling's Western Residence, he said with ease: "When I rise to the three offices, I shall make you my recorder."

units.zh: 父顒，齊中書侍郎，有名於時。
units.en: His father Yan had been a Secretariat Attendant under Qi and was well known in his day.
units.literal: His father Yan was a Secretariat Attendant of Qi and had a reputation in his time.

units.zh: 周捨字昇逸，汝南安城人，晉左光祿大夫顗之八世孫也。
units.en: Zhou She, whose courtesy name was Shengyi, came from Ancheng in Runan and was the eighth-generation descendant of Zhou Yi, who had served Jin as Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
units.literal: Zhou She, styled Shengyi, was a native of Ancheng in Runan and an eighth-generation descendant of Zhou Yi, the Jin Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

units.zh: 捨幼聰潁，顒異之，臨卒謂曰：「汝不患不富貴，但當持之以道德。」
units.en: As a boy, She was quick and clever, and Yan saw something extraordinary in him. On his deathbed Yan told him, "You need not fear that you will lack wealth and rank, but you must hold yourself to moral principle."
units.literal: She in youth was clever and quick; Yan regarded him as exceptional. On his deathbed he told him, "You need not worry about lacking wealth and rank, but you must uphold yourself with moral virtue."

units.zh: 吏部尚書范雲與顒素善，重捨才器，言之於高祖，召拜尚書祠部郎。
units.en: Fan Yun, Minister of Personnel, had long been close to Yan and admired She's ability. He recommended him to the High Ancestor, who summoned She and appointed him Gentleman of the Sacrifices Section in the Secretariat.
units.literal: Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Fan Yun had long been on good terms with Yan and valued She's talent and capacity; he spoke of him to the High Ancestor, who summoned and appointed him Gentleman of the Department of Sacrifices in the Secretariat.

units.zh: 同志者乃共刻石立碑，蔡邕爲其文，旣而謂涿郡盧植曰：「吾爲碑銘多矣，皆有慙德，唯郭有道無愧色耳。」
units.en: His admirers raised a stone stele with an inscription by Cai Yong, who later told Lu Zhi of Zhuojun: "I have composed countless epitaphs, and most leave me uneasy about my own character—only Guo Youdao's leaves me untroubled."
units.literal: Those of like mind then together carved stone and erected a stele; Cai Yong composed its text. Afterwards he said to Lu Zhi of Zhuojun: "I have written many stele inscriptions, and in all I have felt shame for my virtue—only for Guo Youdao do I feel no shame."

units.zh: 明年春，卒于家，時年四十二。
units.en: The following spring he died at home at the age of forty-two.
units.literal: The next spring he died at home, aged forty-two.

units.zh: 永平中，車駕近出，而信陽侯陰就幹突禁衛，車府令徐匡鉤就車，收禦者送獄。
units.en: During Yongping the emperor rode out on a short tour; Marquis Yin Jiu of Xinyang forced his way through the palace guard; carriage-house director Xu Kuang seized his chariot and jailed the charioteer.
units.literal: In the Yongping period, the imperial carriage went out on a near excursion, and Marquis of Xinyang Yin Jiu burst through the forbidden guard; the carriage-house director Xu Kuang hooked Jiu's carriage and arrested the driver and sent him to prison.

units.zh: 良上言曰：『信陽侯就倚恃外戚，幹犯乘輿，無人臣禮，為大不敬。
units.en: Wu Liang memorialized: 'Yin Jiu trades on his status as an imperial in-law, obstructs the imperial train, and shows none of a subject's deference—that is grave disrespect.'
units.literal: Liang submitted words, saying, 'Marquis of Xinyang Jiu relies on being maternal kin, violates the imperial equipage, lacks the ritual of minister and subject, and is greatly irreverent.'

units.zh: 乃令樊噲召高祖。
units.en: He then ordered Fan Kuai to summon Gaozu.
units.literal: He then ordered Fan Kuai to summon Gaozu.

units.zh: 於是樊噲從高祖來。
units.en: So Fan Kuai came to follow Emperor Gaozu.
units.literal: Therefore Fan Kuai followed Gaozu and came.

units.zh: 於是少年豪吏如蕭、曹、樊噲等皆為收沛子弟，得三千人。
units.en: So the young brave officials like Xiao, Cao, Fan Kuai, and others all recruited young men from Pei and gathered three thousand.
units.literal: Therefore young heroic officials like Xiao, Cao, Fan Kuai and others all recruited Pei youths, got three thousand.

units.zh: 樊噲、張良諫，乃封秦重寶財物府庫，還軍霸上。
units.en: Fan Kuai and Zhang Liang remonstrated, so he sealed up Qin's important treasures, property, and treasuries, and returned the army to Bashang.
units.literal: Fan Kuai and Zhang Liang remonstrated, so he sealed up Qin's important treasures, property, and treasuries, and returned the army to Bashang.

units.zh: 樊噲聞事急，直入，怒甚。
units.en: Fan Kuai heard the situation was urgent and charged straight in, extremely angry.
units.literal: Fan Kuai heard the situation was urgent and charged straight in, extremely angry.

units.zh: 有頃，沛公起如廁，招樊噲出，置車官屬，獨騎，與樊噲、靳彊、滕公、紀成步，從間道走軍，使張良留謝羽。
units.en: After a while, Pei Gong rose as if to use the privy and beckoned Fan Kuai out. Leaving his carriages and attendants behind, he rode off alone, while Fan Kuai, Jin Qiang, Lord Teng, and Ji Cheng went on foot. They fled the camp by a side road, and he had Zhang Liang remain to apologize to Xiang Yu.
units.literal: After a while, Pei Gong rose as if to use the toilet and beckoned Fan Kuai to come out. He placed his chariot officials and retainers, rode alone with Fan Kuai, Jin Qiang, Lord Teng, and Ji Cheng on foot, escaping the army by a side road, leaving Zhang Liang to stay and apologize to Xiang Yu.

units.zh: 井丹字大春，扶风郿人也。
units.en: Jing Dan, styled Dachun, came from Mei in Fufeng.
units.literal: Jing Dan, courtesy name Dachun, was a man of Mei in Fufeng.

units.zh: 少受业太学，通《五经》，善谈论，故京师为之语曰：“《五经》纷纶井大春。”
units.en: He studied the Five Classics at the Imperial Academy and shone in debate—hence the capital rhyme: "The Five Classics in glorious tangle—Jing Dachun."
units.literal: In his youth he received instruction at the Imperial Academy, penetrated the Five Classics, and was skilled in discourse; therefore the capital made a saying of him: "The Five Classics in profusion—Jing Dachun."

units.zh: 自是隐闭，不关人事，以寿终。
units.en: After that he barred his gate to the world and died in old age.
units.literal: From this he hid himself and closed his door, not concerning himself with human affairs, and ended his years by natural lifespan.

units.zh: 建武末，沛王辅等五王居北宫，皆好宾客，更遣请丹，不能致。
units.en: Late in Jianwu the five princes, including Prince Liu Fu of Pei, lodged in the Northern Palace; all loved hosting guests and in turn sent to invite Jing Dan, but could not bring him.
units.literal: At the end of Jianwu, Prince Liu Fu of Pei and the other five princes dwelt in the Northern Palace; all loved hosting guests and in turn sent to invite Dan, but could not bring him.

units.zh: 世祖武皇帝情等布衣，寄深同氣。
units.en: Ancestor Emperor Wu treated him as an equal of the robe and bound him with shared blood.
units.literal: Ancestor Emperor Wu treated him as a commoner's equal and entrusted him with the bond of shared blood.

units.zh: 武皇大漸，實奉詔言。
units.en: When Emperor Wu lay dying, I truly received his charge in words.
units.literal: When Emperor Wu fell gravely ill, I truly received his charge in words.

units.zh: 司馬彪
units.en: Sima Biao
units.literal: Sima Biao

units.zh: （司馬彪續作）。
units.en: (continued by Sima Biao)
units.literal: (continued by Sima Biao)

units.zh: 北宋真宗時，有人把晉朝司馬彪的《續漢書》八志三十卷與之合刊，成為今天的《後漢書》。
units.en: During Emperor Zhenzong's reign in the Northern Song, the thirty volumes of eight monographs from Sima Biao's Xu Han Shu of the Jin dynasty were combined with Fan Ye's work, creating the Book of Later Han we know today.
units.literal: During the reign of Emperor Zhenzong of the Northern Song, someone combined the thirty volumes of eight treatises from Sima Biao's 'Xu Han Shu' of the Jin dynasty with it, forming today's 'Book of Later Han'.

units.zh: 〈（《續漢書》作者，有八
units.en: 〈(author of the 'Xu Han Shu', with eight
units.literal: 〈(Author of 'Xu Han Shu', has eight

units.zh: 三十卷補入范曄所著《後漢書》）〉
units.en: thirty volumes that were incorporated into Fan Ye's Book of Later Han〉)
units.literal: thirty volumes supplementing Fan Ye's Book of Later Han〉)

units.zh: (西晉)
units.en: (Western Jin dynasty)
units.literal: (Western Jin)

units.literal: <Treatises>

units.zh: 書中分十紀、八十列傳和八志
units.en: The book consists of ten imperial annals, eighty biographies, and eight monographs
units.literal: The book is divided into ten annals, eighty biographies, and eight treatises

units.zh: 仲長《昌言》，亦其大要。
units.en: Zhongchang Tong's Open Words also states the same essentials.
units.literal: Zhongchang's Open Words also states its great essentials.

units.zh: 幼爲外祖張岱所異，岱常謂諸子曰：「此兒汝家之陽元也。」
units.en: As a boy he impressed his maternal grandfather Zhang Dai, who often told his sons, "This child is the Wei Shu of your family."
units.literal: In childhood he was regarded as extraordinary by his maternal grandfather Zhang Dai, who often told his sons, "This boy is the Yangyuan of your family."

units.zh: 至奚仲為夏車正，建其斿旐，尊卑上下，各有等級。
units.en: When Xi Zhong served the Xia as master of chariots, he standardized streamers and pennants so rank from highest to lowest matched fixed grades.
units.literal: Down to Xi Zhong, who for the Xia was chariot master, setting up his streamers and pennons, noble and base, high and low, each had grades.

units.zh: 伏尋所定五禮，起齊永明三年，太子步兵校尉伏曼容表求制一代禮樂，于時參議置新舊學士十人，止修五禮，諮稟衛將軍丹陽尹王儉，學士亦分住郡中，製作歷年，猶未克就。
units.en: I humbly review the history of the Five Rites now completed: the project began in the third year of Yongming under Qi, when Fu Manrong, Infantry Commandant to the Crown Prince, submitted a memorial requesting the compilation of ritual and music for the age. At that time the court deliberated appointing ten senior and junior academicians to work exclusively on the Five Rites, reporting to Wang Jian, General of the Guard and Intendant of Danyang. The academicians were also dispersed to various commanderies. Years of work passed, yet the project remained unfinished.
units.literal: I humbly examine the fixed Five Rites: they began in the third year of Yongming of Qi, when the Crown Prince's Infantry Commandant Fu Manrong submitted a memorial requesting the compilation of ritual and music for one generation. At that time it was deliberated to appoint ten old and new academicians, restricting the work to the Five Rites, with consultation and reporting to General of the Guard and Intendant of Danyang Wang Jian. The academicians also dispersed to reside in various commanderies. Production continued for years, yet it was still not completed.

units.zh: 文二王 明七王
units.en: The Two Princes of Emperor Wen; The Seven Princes of Emperor Ming
units.literal: Wen's Two Princes; Ming's Seven Princes

units.zh: 明帝十一男：敬皇后生東昏侯寶卷，江夏王寶玄，鄱陽王寶寅，和帝；
units.en: Emperor Ming had eleven sons: Empress Jing bore Bao Juan, Marquis of Donghun; Bao Xuan, Prince of Jiangxia; Bao Yin, Prince of Poyang; and the Emperor He;
units.literal: Emperor Ming had eleven sons: Empress Jing bore the Marquis of Donghun, Bao Juan, the Prince of Jiangxia, Bao Xuan, the Prince of Poyang, Bao Yin, and the Emperor He;

units.zh: 明帝建武二年，通直常侍庾曇隆啓曰：「周定雒邑，天子置畿內之民；
units.en: In the second year of Jianwu (495), Regular Attendant Yu Tanlong memorialized: "When the Zhou fixed their capital at Luoyi, the Son of Heaven settled the people of the capital domain;
units.literal: In the second year of Jianwu under Emperor Ming, Regular Attendant Yu Tanlong submitted: "When the Zhou fixed their capital at Luoyi, the Son of Heaven placed the people of the capital domain;

units.zh: 明帝立，欲以聞喜公遙欣爲荊州，轉昭粲爲右將軍，中書令。
units.en: When Emperor Ming took the throne, intending to appoint Yaoxin, Duke of Wenxi, to Jing Province, he reassigned Zhaocan as General of the Right and Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: When Emperor Ming was established, wishing to make the Duke of Wenxi, Yaoxin, Governor of Jing, he transferred Zhaocan to General of the Right and Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 巴陵隱王寶義字智勇，明帝長子也。
units.en: Bao Yi, Prince Yin of Baling, whose style name was Zhiyong, was Emperor Ming's eldest son.
units.literal: The Prince Yin of Baling, Bao Yi, style name Zhiyong, was Emperor Ming's eldest son.

units.zh: 江夏王寶玄字智深，明帝第三子也。
units.en: Bao Xuan, Prince of Jiangxia, whose style name was Zhishen, was Emperor Ming's third son.
units.literal: The Prince of Jiangxia, Bao Xuan, style name Zhishen, was Emperor Ming's third son.

units.zh: 鄱陽王寶夤字智亮，明帝第六子也。
units.en: Bao Yin, Prince of Poyang, whose style name was Zhiliang, was Emperor Ming's sixth son.
units.literal: The Prince of Poyang, Bao Yin, style name Zhiliang, was Emperor Ming's sixth son.

units.zh: 殷貴嬪生巴陵隱王寶義，晉熙王寶嵩；
units.en: Honored Consort Yin bore Bao Yi, Prince Yin of Baling, and Bao Song, Prince of Jinxing;
units.literal: the Honored Consort Yin bore the Prince Yin of Baling, Bao Yi, and the Prince of Jinxing, Bao Song;

units.zh: 晉熙王寶嵩字智靖，明帝第十子也。
units.en: Bao Song, Prince of Jinxing, whose style name was Zhijing, was Emperor Ming's tenth son.
units.literal: The Prince of Jinxing, Bao Song, style name Zhijing, was Emperor Ming's tenth son.

units.zh: 袁貴妃生廬陵王寶源；
units.en: Honored Consort Yuan bore Bao Yuan, Prince of Luling;
units.literal: the Honored Consort Yuan bore the Prince of Luling, Bao Yuan;

units.zh: 廬陵王寶源字智淵，明帝第五子也。
units.en: Bao Yuan, Prince of Luling, whose style name was Zhiyuan, was Emperor Ming's fifth son.
units.literal: The Prince of Luling, Bao Yuan, style name Zhiyuan, was Emperor Ming's fifth son.

units.zh: 管淑妃生邵陵王寶攸；
units.en: Virtuous Consort Guan bore Bao You, Prince of Shaoling;
units.literal: the Virtuous Consort Guan bore the Prince of Shaoling, Bao You;

units.zh: 邵陵王寶攸字智宣，明帝第九子也。
units.en: Bao You, Prince of Shaoling, whose style name was Zhixuan, was Emperor Ming's ninth son.
units.literal: The Prince of Shaoling, Bao You, style name Zhixuan, was Emperor Ming's ninth son.

units.zh: 許淑媛生桂陽王寶貞。
units.en: Lady of Graceful Demeanor Xu bore Bao Zhen, Prince of Guiyang.
units.literal: the Lady of Graceful Demeanor Xu bore the Prince of Guiyang, Bao Zhen.

units.zh: 桂陽王寶貞，明帝第十一子也。
units.en: Bao Zhen, Prince of Guiyang, was Emperor Ming's eleventh son.
units.literal: The Prince of Guiyang, Bao Zhen, was Emperor Ming's eleventh son.

units.zh: 餘皆早夭。
units.en: All the others died in infancy.
units.literal: The rest all died young.

units.zh: 明子七國，終亦衰亡。
units.en: Ming's seven princely lines likewise ended in ruin.
units.literal: Ming's seven sons and their states in the end also declined and perished.

units.zh: 南齊書卷五十‧列傳第三十一
units.en: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 50 · Biographies 31
units.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 50 · Biographies 31

units.zh: 世祖雖可其奏，以彖言辭依違，大怒，使左丞王逡之奏曰：
units.en: Emperor Wu approved the memorial but was furious because Can's wording was evasive, and he had Left Assistant Director Wang Qunzhi memorialize:
units.literal: The Shizu though he approved the memorial, because Can's words were evasive, was greatly angered and had left director Wang Junzhi memorialize:

units.zh: 祖靈運，宋臨川內史。
units.en: His grandfather Lingyun had been Song governor of Linchuan.
units.literal: His grandfather Lingyun was Song grand administrator of Linchuan.

units.zh: :　　臣聞行父盡忠，無禮斯疾；
units.en: Your servant has heard: a son honors his father with full loyalty — without ritual there is rot;
units.literal: Your servant has heard that a son honors his father with full loyalty — without ritual there is disease;

units.zh: :　　今月九日，治書侍御史臣司馬侃啓彈征北諮議參軍事謝超宗，稱「根性昏動，率心險放，悖議爽眞，囂辭犯實，親朋忍聞，衣冠掩目，輙收付廷尉法獄治罪」。
units.en: On the ninth of this month, your servant Sima Kan, Reviewing Secretary and Attendant Censor, submitted an impeachment against Xie Chaozong, advisory staff officer for the Campaigning-North command, saying: "His root nature is muddled and rash; his heart is dangerous and unrestrained; his perverse arguments violate truth and his clamorous words offend fact. Kin and friends cannot bear to hear him; gentlemen cover their eyes. He should at once be arrested, delivered to the law prison of the Chamberlain for Law Enforcement, and punished for his crime."
units.literal: On the ninth of this month reviewing-secretary censor Sima Kan memorialized northern-campaign adviser Chaozong, saying "his root nature is dull and rash, heart dangerous and unrestrained, rebellious discourse offends truth, arrogant words violate fact — kin and friends cannot bear to hear, caps and gowns cover their eyes — urge seizure and delivery to the tribunal."

units.zh: 臣等參議，請以見事免彖所居官，解兼御史中丞，輙攝曹依舊下禁止視事如故。
units.en: We ask Can be removed and relieved of acting censor, forbidden yet to view affairs as before.
units.literal: Your servants deliberating request that by the present affair Can be removed, relieved of acting censor, and your servant take charge to forbid him yet view affairs as before.

units.zh: :　　治書侍御史臣司馬侃雖承稟有由，而初無疑執，亦合及咎。
units.en: Your servant Sima Kan, Reviewing Secretary and Attendant Censor, had grounds for following orders, but at first he did not hold to any objection; he too should share the blame.
units.literal: Reviewing-secretary censor Sima Kan though he followed orders had at first no doubtful hold — he too should share guilt.

units.zh: 請杖督五十，奪勞百日。
units.en: Request fifty strokes and deprivation of merit for a hundred days.
units.literal: Request staff beating fifty and deprivation of merit a hundred days.

units.zh: 是時，定陶共王愛幸，幾代太子。
units.en: At that time Prince Kang of Dingtao enjoyed the emperor's favor and nearly displaced the crown prince.
units.literal: At that time the Prince of Gong of Dingtao was loved and favored and nearly replaced the heir apparent.

units.zh: 元帝崩，成帝即位，甚敬重商，徙為左將軍。
units.en: After Emperor Yuan died and Emperor Cheng took the throne, the new sovereign held Wang Shang in high regard and appointed him General of the Left.
units.literal: When Emperor Yuan died, Emperor Cheng ascended the throne; he greatly respected Wang Shang and transferred him to be General of the Left.

units.zh: 上於是美壯商之固守，數稱其議。
units.en: The emperor then praised Wang Shang for holding firm and repeatedly commended his counsel.
units.literal: The sovereign thereupon praised and admired Shang's steadfast holding firm, and repeatedly commended his proposal.

units.zh: 天子聞而歎曰：「此真漢相矣！」
units.en: When the emperor heard of it, he sighed and said, 'This truly is a Han chancellor!'
units.literal: The Son of Heaven heard and sighed, saying, 'This is truly a Han chancellor!'

units.zh: 上素重商，知匡言多險，制曰「勿治」。
units.en: The emperor had long respected Wang Shang and recognized Zhang Kuang's memorial for the vicious attack it was, so he ruled, 'Take no further action.'
units.literal: The sovereign had always esteemed Shang; he knew Kuang's words were mostly treacherous, and issued a rescript saying, 'Do not prosecute.'

units.zh: 鳳固爭之，於是制詔御史：「蓋丞相以德輔翼國家，典領百寮，協和萬國，為職任莫重焉。
units.en: Wang Feng would not let the matter drop, and the emperor had to issue an edict to the censor-in-chief: 'The chancellor exists to support the dynasty with moral authority, to head the bureaucracy, and to keep the realm in harmony—no burden is weightier.
units.literal: Feng firmly disputed it; thereupon an edict was issued to the imperial secretary: 'In general the chancellor with virtue assists and wings the state, presides over the host of officials, harmonizes the myriad states—of offices and duties none is heavier.

units.zh: 今樂昌侯商為丞相，出入五年，未聞忠言嘉謀，而有不忠執左道之辜，陷於大辟。
units.en: Yet in five years as chancellor, Lechang Marquis Wang Shang has offered no loyal counsel worthy of the name, while the charge of disloyalty and heterodox conduct would carry the death penalty.
units.literal: Now Lechang Marquis Shang has been chancellor, going in and out five years; loyal words and fine plans have not been heard from him, yet there is the guilt of disloyalty and holding to the left path, falling into great execution.

units.zh: 前商女弟內行不修，奴賊殺人，疑商教使，為商重臣，故抑而不窮。
units.en: Earlier his younger sister's private conduct was scandalous: a household slave committed murder, and some suspected Wang Shang ordered it. Because he was a pillar of the court, I suppressed the case and did not press to the bottom.
units.literal: Earlier Shang's younger sister's conduct within was not cultivated; a slave villainously killed a person; there was suspicion Shang instructed and sent him; because Shang was a weighty minister, therefore it was suppressed and not fully investigated.

units.zh: 今或言商不以自悔而反怨懟，朕甚傷之。
units.en: Now I am told he shows no remorse but nurses grievance instead. That wounds me deeply.
units.literal: Now some say Shang does not thereby repent himself but instead harbors resentment; We are greatly wounded by it.

units.zh: 惟商與先帝有外親，未忍致於理。
units.en: Yet Wang Shang is tied to the late emperor by marriage, and I cannot bring myself to subject him to full criminal process.
units.literal: Only, Shang has outer kinship with the late emperor; We have not been able to bear bringing him to the law.

units.zh: 其赦商罪。
units.en: I therefore pardon his offenses.
units.literal: Let Shang's crimes be pardoned.

units.zh: 使者收丞相印綬。」
units.en: Envoys shall relieve him of the chancellor's seal and sash.'
units.literal: Let envoys collect the chancellor's seal and ribbon.'

units.zh: 太子由是遂爲嗣矣。
units.en: The crown prince was thereby secured as successor.
units.literal: The heir apparent thereby became the successor.

units.zh: 元帝竟崩，成帝初即位，擢丹爲長樂衛尉，遷右將軍，賜爵關內侯，食邑三百戶，給事中，後徙左將軍、光祿大夫。
units.en: When Emperor Yuan died and Emperor Cheng first succeeded, Shi Dan was promoted to Commandant of the Chang'le Palace Guard, then General of the Right, granted Marquis within the Pass with a three-hundred-household fief and palace attendance, and later moved to General of the Left and Grand Master of the Household.
units.literal: Emperor Yuan finally died; when Emperor Cheng first ascended the throne, Dan was promoted to Commandant of the Chang'le Palace Guard, transferred to General of the Right, granted rank as Marquis within the Pass with a fief of three hundred households, given palace attendance, and later moved to General of the Left and Grand Master of the Household.

units.zh: 鴻嘉元年，上遂下詔曰：「夫褒有德，賞元功，古今通義也。
units.en: In Hongjia 1 the emperor issued an edict: "Honoring the virtuous and rewarding great service is a principle honored in every age.
units.literal: In the first year of Hongjia the sovereign then issued an edict saying: "To praise those with virtue and reward primary merit is the common principle of antiquity and the present.

units.zh: 左將軍丹往時導朕以忠正，秉義醇一，舊德茂焉。
units.en: General of the Left Shi Dan long ago guided Us with loyal uprightness, held to pure integrity, and his old merit is abundant.
units.literal: General of the Left Dan in former times guided Us with loyalty and uprightness, held righteousness pure and single, and old virtue flourished therein.

units.zh: 其封丹爲武陽侯，國東海郯之武強聚，戶千一百。」
units.en: Let Shi Dan be enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuyang, with a fief at Wuqiang in Tan county, Donghai commandery, of eleven hundred households."
units.literal: Let Dan be enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuyang, with his state at Wuqiang village in Tan of Donghai, one thousand one hundred households."

units.zh: 為將軍前後十六年，永始中病乞骸骨，上賜策曰：「左將軍寢病不衰，願歸治疾，朕愍以官職之事久留將軍，使躬不瘳。
units.en: He served sixteen years as a general. In the Yongshi period he fell ill and asked to retire. The emperor replied: 'Your illness as General of the Left does not improve, and you wish to go home to heal. I regret that state business has kept you at your post so long that your health has not mended.
units.literal: Serving as general before and after sixteen years, in the Yongshi era he was ill and begged for his bones; the sovereign bestowed a rescript saying: 'General of the Left, your lying illness does not wane; you wish to return to treat illness; We pity that the affairs of office have long detained the general, causing your person not to recover.

units.zh: 使光祿勳賜將軍黃金五十斤，安車駟馬，其上將軍印綬。
units.en: Send the superintendent of the imperial household with fifty catties of gold, a comfortable carriage and team of four, and take your seal and sash as general.
units.literal: Let the superintendent of the imperial household be sent to bestow on the general fifty jin of gold, a secure carriage and four horses; let him present the general's seal and ribbon.

units.zh: 宜專精神，務近醫藥，以輔不衰。」
units.en: Devote yourself to rest and medical care so that your strength may return.'
units.literal: You should concentrate spirit, devote yourself to drawing near to physicians and medicine, in order to assist non-declining.'

units.zh: 車駕三朝率百僚舉哀于朝堂，一依魏明帝服山陽公故事。
units.en: For three days the emperor led all officials in mourning at the court hall, following entirely the precedent of Emperor Ming of Wei mourning the Duke of Shanyang.
units.literal: For three days the emperor led all officials in mourning at the court hall, following entirely the precedent of Emperor Ming of Wei mourning the Duke of Shanyang.

units.zh: 左丞徐爰案司馬孚議皇后不稱姓，春秋逆王后于齊，澄不引典據明，而以意立議，坐免官，白衣領職。
units.en: Left Assistant Xu Ai cited Sima Fu's argument that the empress does not use her surname, and that in the Spring and Autumn Annals the queen was met and escorted from Qi. Cheng failed to cite clear classical evidence and instead based his position on personal opinion; for this he was dismissed from office and served in plain clothes while retaining his duties.
units.literal: Left Assistant Xu Ai cited Sima Fu's discussion that the empress does not use her surname, and that in Spring and Autumn the queen was met and escorted from Qi. Cheng did not cite classic evidence clearly but established the discussion by personal opinion; on this account he was removed from office and served in plain clothes while retaining his duties.
